name: Image representation benchmarking (representative benchmarking)
description: By leveraging contrastive learning, clustering, and other pretext tasks, unsupervised methods for learning image representations have reached impressive results on standard benchmarks. The result has been a crowded field - many methods with substantially different implementations yield results that seem nearly identical on popular benchmarks, such as linear evaluation on ImageNet. However, a single result does not tell the whole story. In this paper, we compare methods using performance-based benchmarks such as linear evaluation, nearest neighbor classification, and clustering for several different datasets, demonstrating the lack of a clear front-runner within the current state-of-the-art. In contrast to prior work that performs only supervised vs. unsupervised comparison, we compare several different unsupervised methods against each other. To enrich this comparison, we analyze embeddings with measurements such as uniformity, tolerance, and centered kernel alignment (CKA), and propose two new metrics of our own: nearest neighbor graph similarity and linear prediction overlap. We reveal through our analysis that in isolation, single popular methods should not be treated as though they represent the field as a whole, and that future work ought to consider how to leverage the complimentary nature of these methods. We also leverage CKA to provide a framework to robustly quantify augmentation invariance, and provide a reminder that certain types of invariance will be undesirable for downstream tasks.
evaluation_method: Linear evaluation accuracy (ImageNet), nearest-neighbor accuracy, clustering metrics (e.g., NMI), representation similarity metrics (CKA), plus proposed metrics (nearest neighbor graph similarity, linear prediction overlap)
general_score_metric: Linear evaluation accuracy on ImageNet (supplemented by NMI and CKA for deeper analysis)
typical_sota_score: 60–85% (linear-evaluation accuracy ranges reported across unsupervised methods depending on protocol and model)
reputation: An influential comparative study in the representation learning community that highlighted limitations of single-metric evaluations and introduced additional analysis tools; cited by researchers studying unsupervised features.
notes: Non-LLM, multi-metric benchmark; ImageNet linear-evaluation can be saturated and sensitive to evaluation protocol (augmentation, epoch, backbone). The suite emphasizes complementary diagnostics beyond a single aggregate score.
